First published in 1584, with title: The copie of a leter, vvryten by a master of arte of Cambridge, to his friend in London. Has been erroneously ascribed to Robert Parsons. "Leicesters commonwealth" is a political tract against Elizabeth Is government. It went through many stages and forms, both in manuscript and in print, and is most well known by the title "Leicesters commonwealth". It was first printed on the continent in 1584 with title "The copie of a leter, wryten by a master of arte of Cambridge, to his friend in London". It was formerly attributed to Robert Parsons and is sometimes attributed to Thomas Morgan. Cf. DNB s.v. Dudley, Robert, Earl of Leicester. 1532?-1588. "Leicesters commonwealth" was republished in 1641 and was versified as "Leicesters ghost" about the same time. Leather. Bound together with Leicester's Ghost. P. 102 called 103 and 103 called 102; same for 118-119. P. 120 called 110. Stamp of Vernon J. Watney, Cornbury.

metadata.description: The 1692 Jamaica earthquake struck Port Royal, Jamaica, on 7 June. A stopped pocket watch indicated that it occurred around 11:43 AM local time. Known as the "storehouse and treasury of the West Indies" and as "one of the wickedest places on Earth", Port Royal was, at the time, the unofficial capital of Jamaica and one of the busiest and wealthiest ports in the Americas, as well as a common home port for many of the privateers and pirates operating on the Caribbean Sea. The 1692 earthquake caused most of the city to sink below sea level. About 2,000 people died as a result of the earthquake and the following tsunami, and another 3,000 people died in the following days due to injuries and disease. This book "The Port Royal 1692 Disaster" details the history before, during and after that great earthquake.

metadata.description: Who We Are. Stories of American Families is a story of nine families that blended through marriage and other relationships over the centuries into a current 21st century family, the family of William Dennis Hendricson, that’s me, and my wife, Susan Lienau Hendricson. As these families evolved over time, they cross paths with the famous and infamous who are highlighted in the stories told in this book: Willem Frederic George Lodewijk van der Dussen, a founding father of modern genealogy in Europe and first chronicler of Hendricson family history; Maarten Schenck Van Nydeggan Hendriksz, one of Europe’s most villainous mercenary soldiers and Lambert Barentse Hendriksz, Holland’s most revered naval hero; Peter Stuyvesant, peg-legged soldier-politician leader of the New Amsterdam colony; legendary pirate of the Caribbean Captain Henry Morgan; ill-fated Miles Morgan, vanished in the Carolina’s a decade before the Lost Colony of Roanoke; Molly Reeve Webster, the Witch of Hadley, catalyst for the Salem Witch Trials; and her nemesis, scientist, public health champion and witchcraft-monger, Cotton Mather; the mystic idealist, William Penn, whose political concepts guided Jefferson, Franklin and other founding fathers; George Washington, need I say more; Daniel Boone; legendary frontiersman; Molly Pitcher, Revolutionary War heroine; General Daniel Morgan, hero of Saratoga and Cowpens in the Revolutionary War; British General Charles Cornwallis, the most renowned Redcoat commander of the Revolutionary War; Moses Black Harris, famed Mountain Man of the American West; Abner Doubleday, Civil War General and rumored founder of baseball; WZ Ripley, a catalyst for 20th century White Supremacy dogma; Ernie Davis, Heisman Trophy winning college football player; George Preston Marshall, key founder of the National Football League in the U.S. and ardent segregationist; Howard Cosell, America’s leading sports journalist in the 1970s; John Lewis, prominent U.S. Civil Rights leader; and Shirley Povich, Pulitzer prize winning sportswriter, with guest appearances by other notables including Christopher Columbus, on his first approach to the Americas, Roger Maris, U.S. baseball legend, the rock band Blood, Sweat and Tears, voting rights advocate Evelyn T. Butts, rockabilly and country western star Jerry Lee Lewis, and best-selling author of “On Death and Dying,” Elizabeth Kubler-Ross. However, Who We Are. Stories of American Families does not center on these luminaries; they make cameo appearances, engaging various family members, past and present, in unique experiences, or serving as catalysts for societal phenomenon that influenced the lives of these individuals. Instead, Who We Are is about people who did the best they could to build a safe, happy and prosperous life for themselves in America beginning in the 17th century. The individuals in the nine families who first immigrated to America were average folk, working class for the most part, with no royal connections or inherited wealth to prop them up. Two of the original immigrants came from merchant families that previously had accrued wealth in Europe, but through misfortune, inexplicable decisions, and political turmoil, had drifted so far away from prosperity that America was seen as their only recourse. Other original immigrants were from families that had known only the meager existence of tenant farm labor for generations. The first immigrants in two other families arrived on legal missions as young, unmarried men, and elected to seek their fortune in America rather than return to uncertain futures in Europe. Who We Are tells the stories of the people in these nine families before and after their arrival in America. All families have extraordinary stories, and collectively, these stories shape society. William D. Hendricson June 24, 2026

metadata.creator: Marsland, William David
description: ix, 277 pages : 22 cm

Venezuela's history is a pageant in which have passed some of the world's most fascinating figures: Christopher Columbus, who mistook Venezuela for the Garden of Eden; Sir Walter Raleigh, whose death warrant was signed on the banks of the Orinoco; Henry Morgan, who made his exciting escape from Lake Maracaibo by firing the Spanish fleet ; Simon Bolivar, who liberated a continent; Antonio Guzman Blanco, history's most spectacular swindler. Most extraordinary of all, perhaps, was Francisco de Miranda, a conceit of Venezuelan culture, who became an habitue of Europe's courts and bordellos. Friend of Alexander Hamilton, intimate of Catherine the Great, a general of the French Revolution, and a conspirator in the pay of William Pitt, Miranda was determined to free his country, singlehanded if need be. In 1806, despite the warnings of President Thomas Jefferson and Secretary of State James Madison, he recruited an army of young Americans in New York for an invasion of Venezuela. The attack failed. Fifty of the Americans rotted in Spanish dungeons. Ten were executed, their bloody heads displayed on spikes. In death, they became some of the first martyrs to Latin American independence. Today Venezuela is in the full tide of economic development. She is a new country, like our own; and she is also a melting pot. African Negroes and American Indians, together with European whites, have contributed their bodies, superstitions, languages, and temperaments to form a distinct cultural pattern completely different from any of the civilizations that produced it. Venezuela is a prince-or-pauper country -- a country of incalculable potential. What happens to that potential is a matter of intense concern to every American. While oil from Maracaibo and iron ore from the Gran Sabana feed United States refineries and steel mills, Venezuela is vital to hemispheric defense. In this book, the first history of Venezuela in English, the reader will find a colorful and enlightening study of a nation in the making. - Jacket flap

metadata.description: Ancient Society, or Researches in the Lines of Human Progress from Savagery, Through Barbarism to Civilization is a significant contribution to studies of cultural anthropology. Its author, Lewis Henry Morgan, was an American statesman, anthropologist and critic of materialism. Ancient Society develops Morgan's theory of the three stages of human progress, which he theorizes progressed from Savagery through Barbarism to Civilization. Morgan's goal was to trace the advance of human development from different branches of the human family. He uses Greek, Roman and Native American family structure to explain the evolution of family. Morgan conceived of human development as units called ethna, which are similar to inventions, discoveries and domestic institutions. In his book, he traces ethna beginning at subsistence living, then to establishment of government, development of language, and the various forms of family. The final ethna are religion, house and architecture, and property. Morgan was a critic of the Three-Stage theories of history, and the book discusses why he believed that classifying different eras into bronze, stone, etc. was inadequate as a measure of human progress. Morgan was America's most influential social critic. His work was cited by Karl Marx, Friedrich Engels, Charles Darwin, and Sigmund Freud. Ancient Society, or Researches in the Lines of Human Progress from Savagery, Through Barbarism to Civilization is a compelling book for intellectual readers and those interested in a new way of looking at human development.

Cnty.,  No. B332617 (Cal. Ct. App. Jul. 1, 2024) . Facts and Circumstances Julia Bates (Lucas County Prosecutor) : "Anthony Pizza was a hero. He was a tremendous mentor. He was a fierce fighter of crime. He was loving to his family. I guess his legacy is incredible. His legacy will survive as one of greatness, an advocate of victims, and truly a scholar of law." Lynn Balshone Jacobs (Ohio Bar No. 32906)  worked in the  Lucas County Prosecutor's office . Frank Jacobs (Eastman & Smith) and  John Dominic Alessio (Procopio, Cory, Hargreaves & Savitch, LLP)  have fiduciary positions. Frank Jacobs (Ohio Bar No. 11310)  and John Dominic Alessio (California Bar No. 174900) have undue influence. Frank David Jacobs (Ohio Bar No. 11310)  has a disciplinary history (dual representation). Chief Justice Thomas Moyer (Ohio Supreme Court) concurred with the judgment of the court of appeals in State v. S.R, 63 Ohio St. 3d 590, 589 N.E.2d 1319 (Ohio 1992). Chief Justice Thomas Moyer (Ohio Supreme Court): "I would suspend Frank Jacobs for six months and stay the suspension on the condition that he commit no further misconduct during that term." John Dominic Alessio  (California Bar No. 174900) is the managing partner of Procopio, Cory, Hargreaves & Savitch, LLP John S. Alessio was "a force in California politics, serving as an adviser and fund-raiser for Gov. Edmund G. (Pat) Brown. In the 1970's, John Alessio was convicted of income tax evasion and spent two years in Federal prison." Dominic John Alessio: "While I recognize that the reputational damage can never be completely overcome, it would give me great personal pride to have the stigma of a felony conviction removed from my name." Lenard Wolf, Federal Bureau of Investigations: "That’s his nature to make friends with big people . . . That’s the way Dominic John Alessio operates. You know, scratch my back, I’ll scratch your back. Butter up people who can do favors for you when you need them." A. David Stutz, Internal Revenue Service: "That's their style. That’s the Alessio style. That's the way they do business." Thomas William Turner Jr. (California Bar No. #107760) : "John Dominic Alessio is a highly respected attorney, both for his legal skills and his practice management. He has demonstrated as a Management Committee member great judgment, a solid grip on the workings of the firm, as well as a good feel for the legal community and the overall business of law. Perhaps most importantly, John has demonstrated time and again that his decision-making process is driven first and foremost by determining what is in the best interest of the firm as a whole. He will not just succeed, but excel, as Procopio's next Managing Partner." John Dominic Alessio  confirmed his legal representation of Doctor Zubie Moorjani (Medical Board #35.034433, Emeritus) on September 20, 2021. John Dominic Alessio should know that Frank Jacobs (Ohio Bar No. 11310) has a disciplinary history (dual representation).  John Dominic Alessio  and Sunil Moorjani are former classmates at the University of San Diego School of Law (’94). John Dominic Alessio was the sole attorney of record in San Diego Superior Court Case Number 37-2021-00033119-CU-OR-CTL. Theresa Guy (Pillsbury Winthrop) : "As members of the California Bar, we may not represent  conflicting interests  except with the informed written consent of all clients concerned." John Dominic Alessio is a member of the California bar; therefore, he should have recognized the  conflict of interest , and he should have declined to represent the defendants. John Dominic Alessio made false statements to  Mary Wright (California Bar No. 142886)  more than four (4) months after Doctor Zubie Moorjani's statements on May 18, 2021. John Dominic Alessio made false statements to  Mary Wright (California Bar No. 142886)  more than four (4) months after the elder abuse notification to Seema Moorjani and Sunil Moorjani on May 20, 2021. Deepak Moorjani (venture capitalist) : "Additionally, I would like Adult Protective Services of San Diego to investigate John Alessio (Bar No. 174900) for elder abuse. As a member of the California bar, John Alessio is currently the managing partner of Procopio, Cory, Hargreaves & Savitch, LLP (“Procopio”). John Alessio and Sunil Moorjani are former classmates at the University of San Diego Law School (’94), and John Alessio may have allowed a personal relationship to compromise his legal judgment. As a member of the California bar, John Alessio should have recognized the conflict of interest, and he should have declined to represent the defendants. The attached Notification: Suicide Risk is dated January 10, 2019, and this letter was sent via certified mail to Rosemarie Osowik, MD with a cc: to Jennifer Compton of Sun Federal, Louise Jackson of Eastman & Smith, and Sunil Moorjani. Additional, this letter was sent via certified mail to Thomas Osowik, a judge in the Ohio Sixth District Court of Appeals." Greg Lievers (California Bar No. 118037) : "We are going to dismiss without prejudice. A Request for Dismissal will be filed today. My client takes this step in good faith and hopes that it will lead to a cooperative and constructive dialogue with your clients regarding the future care of  Doctor Zubie Moorjani ." Petitioner believes the  Motion to Disqualify John Dominic Alessio et al.  provides the basis for a criminal investigation. John Dominic Alessio (California Bar No. 174900)  is credited with messages from Procopio staff (Kristina Terlaga, Maria Vizcaino, Melissa Avitia Turpin, Zagros Bassirian).

description: 1 online resource (x, 291 pages) :

It is commonplace today to suggest that gender is socially constructed, that the roles women and men fulfill in their daily lives have been created and defined for them by society and social institutions. But how have men and women negotiated and navigated the gender roles that have been thrust upon them? With Gendered Pasts, Kathryn McPherson, Cecilia Morgan, and Nancy M. Forestell have collected eleven engaging essays that seek to answer this question in a wide-ranging exploration of specific gendered dimensions of nineteenth- and twentieth-century Canadian history.The contributors cover all manner of topics related to gender and history across Canada, including: female vagrancy; gambling, drinking, and sex; the role of the miner's wife; the portrayal of gay men; and the sharply defined role of nurses. Unusual in its breadth, Gendered Pasts is essential to the understanding of the various threads and themes in Canadian gender history.Previously published by Oxford University Press
Includes bibliographical references

metadata.description: Meeting the growing global demand for agricultural products requires the development and use of ecologically-based strategies that will allow sustainable intensification based on ecosystem services. An important component of this approach is conservation biological control. This approach encompasses a variety of management practices that protect natural enemy populations in the agro-ecosystem and enhance their fitness and ultimate impact on pests. It represents an alternative to dependence on pesticides which is associated with environmental damage and risks to human health. The interventions used to achieve conservation biological control are commonly based on managing vegetation patterns at the local scale (e.g. flowering strips that promote parasitoids by supplying nectar) or at wider scale (e.g., woodland to serve as donor habitat for natural enemies). Importantly, such vegetation management also offers scope to provide agriculture with additional ecosystem services as diverse as pollination and carbon sequestration. Despite these attractive features and the success of a small number of conservation biological control strategies, it remains underutilized. We identify as barriers to adoption the relative complexity of conservation biological control and challenges with economic evaluation, as well as perceptions and communication. Climate change is a challenge that will demand the development of flexible strategies that can respond to changes in pest distributions and/or food web structure.

metadata.description: Logbook of a whaling voyage to the Atlantic Ocean. Includes descriptions of whales seen or taken, accidents, desertions, illnesses, punishments, and fights. Also contains whale stamps, anchor sketches, a history of the vessel, and a crew list. The keeper reports several instances where members of the crew were drunk. One man list two of his fingers in an accident on October 27, 1875. One man died at St. Helena on 24 March after a stay in the hospital. One man was drunk on 13 December 1876, got into a fight, and was put in irons as a result. The vessel appeared to borrow frequently from other ships she met at sea. Whaling grounds include the 36/36, Western Islands, San Antonio, Cornell, Coast of Africa, Carroll, and Dominica grounds.; Old Dartmouth Historical Society (ODHS 210); Whaling vessel out of New Bedford, Mass., mastered by Charles H. metadata.description: Logbook of a whaling voyage to the Atlantic Ocean. Includes descriptions of types of whales seen or taken, accidents, a death at sea, desertions, shipwrecks, taking on provisions while in port, a stowaway, and illnesses (including scurvy). Also contains whale stamps, whale sketches, a crew list, oil stowed down, and a poem. The ship picked up a barrel of "caraceen" [kerosene] oil on July 2, 1866.The keeper notes that a ship was in quarantine at Santa Cruz on September 12, 1866. The keeper reported that the vessel began leaking in 1867 and continued to do so throughout the remainder of the voyage. Multiple entries note that the captain was sick in 1867, and the vessel was not allowed to land at Faial without quarantining for five days in August 1867. Three men were injured on 31 October 1867. Two whaleboats were stove by whales, two men were killed, and three others were hurt on December 2, 1867. Found three stowaways onboard on 16 April 1868 after leaving Santa Catarina (Brazil). Whaling grounds include the Western Island, Cornell, River Platte, and Western grounds.; Old Dartmouth Historical Society (ODHS 26); Whaling vessel out of New Bedford, Mass., mastered by Andrew M. metadata.description: Logbook of a whaling voyage to the North Pacific and Arctic Oceans and Okhotsk Sea. Includes descriptions of types of whales seen or taken, deaths at sea, accidents at sea, gales, illnesses, desertions, interactions with natives, shipboard medicine for the captain, and throwing tryworks overboard. Also contains whale stamps, a list of provisions, and inventories of whale oil and bone. In 1849 the captain left the ship at Maui due to sickness and was replaced by Eber Almy. There were various accidents aboard the ship, including stove whaleboats, and deaths, including Thomas Howland who was killed by a whale in March 1849. metadata.description: Logbook of a whaling voyage to the South Atlantic and west coast of Africa. Includes descriptions of whales seen or taken, accidents, desertions, and rescues. metadata.creator: Abigail (Ship);Zephyr (Ship);William Hathaway Reynard;Abraham Gardner; Michael Cumiskey
metadata.description: Journal, kept by Michael Cumiskey, of two whaling voyages. First voyage partially documents the Abigail (Ship) of New Bedford, Mass., mastered by William Hathaway Reynard, from 4 April 1836 – 6 November 1838 to the Pacific Ocean. Includes descriptions of whales seen or taken, accidents at sea, desertions, illnesses, fires on ships, mutinous behavior, encounters with natives, rescues, and scrimshaw. Also contains a crew list, poetry, religious verses, and prayers. The keeper was the boat steerer. The crew list is in the front of the book as well as a listing of who raised the whales. The first five months of the voyage are missing. On several occasions early in the journal, the ship was smoked to combat rats. There was a slight mutiny on May 25, 1837. The keeper gives a full-page account in October 1837 of the burning of the English whaleship James Colvin that was set on fire by its jealous cook (who eventually slit his own throat) whose wife and daughter were on board. Second voyage documents the Zephyr (Ship) of New Bedford, Mass., mastered by Abraham Gardner, from 29 June 1838 – 19 March 1843 to the South Pacific and Indian Ocean. Includes descriptions of whales seen or taken, accidents at sea, illnesses, deaths at sea, punishment, and women onboard. Also contains a crew list, provisions, religious verses, and prayers. The ship lost 5 boats in the Indian Ocean as a result of a heavy gale. The crew received word of the murder of two missionaries by natives on February 10, 1840. On February 25, 1840, the steward attacked the captain and was punished. On April 25, 1840, while at Tahiti, one crewman "not being in his right mind" jumped overboard and drowned. The crew list is at the back of the book as well as a list of who raised whales. There are also numerous verses, prayers and references to the Scriptures. After seven months out the ship got its first whale. There were passengers from Oahu to New Bedford, including Reverend Dr. Lafon, his lady, and native servants. Dr. Lafon held church services every Sunday on the voyage home.

The Titanic disaster was the result of a deliberate act of revenge by a brilliant psychotic genius an act of sabotage that was too unthinkable to be considered by forensic investigators in 1912. Dangerous Betrayal: The Vendetta That Sank Titanic traces the historical clashes and unbridled hatred between business and technical giants at the turn of the twentieth century, leading to an outrageous plot to target Titanic. The clever melding of fact and fiction appeals to Titanic aficionados as well as to the conspiracy theorist in each of us as it raises questions never before asked about the worst peacetime maritime accident in history: How could a well-designed ship, equipped with the latest technology, manned by an uber-experienced crew, come to such a terrible end on her first voyage?

"On a voyage to New Earth, the starship Rolling Thunder is powered by an energy no one understands except for its eccentric inventor, Jubal Broussard. Like many of the ship's inhabitants, Jubal rests in a state of suspended animation for years at a time, asleep yet never aging. The moments when Jubal emerges from suspended animation are usually a cause for celebration for his family, including his twin daughters--Cassie and Polly--and their uncle who is captain of the Rolling Thunder. But this time, Jubal makes a shocking announcement: The ship must stop, or everyone will die. These words from the mission's founder, the man responsible for the very existence of the Rolling Thunder, will send shock waves throughout the starship--and divide its passengers into those who believe and those who doubt. And it will be up to Cassie and Polly to stop a mutiny, discover the truth, and usher the ship into a new age of exploration"--

"Howard Marks was released from Terre Haute Penitentiary, Indiana, in April 1995 after serving seven years of a twenty-five year sentence for marijuana smuggling. It was time for a change of career. So he wrote two bestselling books, became a sports writer and travel writer, stood as a parliamentary candidate in Norwich North, Norwich South, Southampton Test and Neath, applied to become the country's Drug Czar, and embarked on a long-running, sellout series of one-man shows." "While performing in his home town of Kenfig Hill, he fell among old friends who made extraordinary claims for Welsh culture. Was Elvis really Welsh? Was there really a tribe of Welsh-speaking Native Americans? At the same time his elderly aunt told him of his outlaw ancestry: William Owen, the legendary Welsh smuggler, who had operated for some time in South America and his great-great-grandfather Patrick McCarty, the half-brother of Billy the Kid, who had joined Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid in Patagonia. He decided to explore South America." "His travels took him to Jamaica and Panama in the footsteps of the Welsh buccaneer Henry Morgan; he went to Brazil looking for groups of Welsh settlers so obscure he never found them, although he did succeed in finding his musical idol Jimmy Page; and he searched among the thriving Welsh community in Patagonia for signs of Billy the Kid's half-brother."--Jacket

Leur cinquième mission? Effectuer un reportage sur Roatan, une île du Honduras, qui fut un important repaire de pirates. L'illustre capitaine Henry Morgan y a vécu quelque temps et on dit qu'il y aurait même enterré son trésor! En suivant la trace des archéologues (particulièrement celle de Mitchell Hedges, qui aurait découvert des objets étranges qu'il soupçonnait de provenir de l'Atlantide), les jeunes voyageurs se lancent dans une expédition périlleuse. Cette dernière prend en effet un tournant aussi inquiétant que palpitant le jour où les jeunes se laissent surprendre par le coucher de soleil lors d'une balade en kayak et se voient contraints de passer la nuit dans une mangrove. Cernés par les dangers, ils y multiplient toutefois les découvertes fabuleuses, guidés par un homme étrange qui apparaît et disparaît sans crier gare..."--SDM

"Un roman d'aventures cousu de fil blanc et teinté d'un soupçon de fantastique, mais prétexte à une exploration ludique des îles du Honduras marquées par l'histoire de la piraterie. Les rebondissements s'enchaînent à bon rythme au gré d'une narration portée par une écriture très graphique qui sert très bien le propos en favorisant un plongeon saisissant au coeur d'une mangrove fourmillante de tarentules, de serpents et d'autres bêtes que l'on croise comme si on y était... Détente."--SDM

In August 1781 Alistair Douglas is sent by the British spy network the Decipherers to York Town in the American Colonies. He is tasked with assisting the Loyalist colonists of Virginia to organize themselves into a militia and fight the Revolutionaries on behalf of the King. Douglas goes undercover as a grain merchant aboard a French military vessel in Chesapeake Bay, where he discovers that matters have progressed much further than anyone in London had imagined ... While Lord Cornwallis turns all his efforts to fortifying York Town, Douglas intercepts disturbing correspondence suggesting that they might be protecting themselves in the wrong place. When a British father and son, Cable and David Morgan, are captured by the French as spies, matters turn critical. Douglas is determined to do whatever it takes to save them, knowing that if he can get them back they might just have a chance to reverse British fortunes before it's too late ..

Straining to keep the US economy at the pinnacle of world influence, President Chuck Lowery is doing what it takes to keep his Economic Revolution on track. Lowery's closest advisors feed the market the financial information that drives confidence and stock market prices higher and higher. Kirby Haines' partnership prospects at Morgan Greenville get better and better as the firm posts record revenue, led by its proprietary trading desk and Harrison Teasedale, a man with an uncanny ability to know how to score big in any trading environment. But Bert Washington can't come to grips with the economy that he and his family experience everyday. His suspicions rekindle an old relationship with John Aichenhead, an FBI agent, who uncovers a conspiracy of epic proportions. A Standard Deviation exposes the unholy Washington Beltway - Wall Street alliance with frightening allusion to the recent real-life meltdown that nearly brought down the nation
